name: shot2code v0.3.2
body_html:
Critical update safety

v0.3.2 protects upgrades that start from older clients. The NSIS installer now stops and verifies the installed backend process tree before any file replacement, including orphan Copilot/Chromium descendants. Matching is scoped to the installed backend path, so unrelated same-name processes are not terminated. If shutdown cannot be verified, installation aborts before replacement and writes %TEMP%\shot2code-installer-preinstall.log.

A genuine public v0.3.0 client was updated to v0.3.2 while a backend descendant deliberately held pydantic_core locked. The installer terminated the installed tree, preserved an unrelated control process, installed completely, force-relaunched, and returned healthy backend/capabilities with matching native hashes.

Models from every provider

  • Choose one or more models from GitHub Copilot, OpenAI, Anthropic/Claude, and Google Gemini.
  • Copilot models are discovered live from the signed-in plan; API-key providers use maintained validated catalogues.
  • One generated option per selected model, within the existing variant limit.
  • Persisted selection migration, stale/deprecated model warnings, media-capability filtering, provider-specific credentials, and retry/history preservation.
  • New credential-safe /api/models catalogue endpoint; secrets are never returned.

Preview, History, and responsive UX

  • Fixed-width 100% desktop previews are centred on a neutral framed backdrop.
  • User-facing Versions navigation is now consistently History.
  • Tablet and mobile layouts expose a separate labelled History destination beside Preview and Chat.
  • Improved preview controls, History row semantics, focus visibility, target sizes, contrast, and reflow.
  • Updated screenshots show the current UI and all-provider model picker.

Windows robustness

  • Prompt-preview diagnostics are safe on strict cp1252 Windows consoles and cannot crash generation on Unicode text.
  • Installer lifecycle and pre-install safeguards have six automated desktop tests.

Validation

  • Backend: 514 passed, 13 skipped.
  • Frontend: 357 passed, 6 skipped; TypeScript and Vite build passed.
  • Desktop: 6/6 updater/installer tests passed.
  • Responsive browser checks covered 352 through 1920 pixels in light and dark modes.
  • Final packaged health, capabilities, model catalogue/provider groups, centred Preview and History UI passed.
  • ZIP/NSIS integrity, full blockmap coverage, MSI extraction, 58 .pyd modules, and native backend hashes passed.

Downloads

  • EXE: recommended per-user installer with automatic updates.
  • MSI: per-machine managed deployment.
  • ZIP: portable build.
  • SHA256SUMS.txt: checksum verification.

The Windows binaries are unsigned and may trigger SmartScreen.

Canonical source release: https://github.com/ArasaniRohithReddy/shot2code/releases/tag/v0.3.2

name: shot2code v0.1.9
body_html:
React and Preact results can now be exported as a real Vite project.

Install

Existing installs update themselves. For a fresh install:

File Use
shot2code-0.1.9-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.9-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

Export as a real project

Choosing Project folder from the download button now depends on the stack:

React / Preact get an actual Vite project:

index.html
src/App.jsx          your component
src/main.jsx         the render call
src/index.css        Tailwind directives
package.json  vite.config.js  tailwind.config.js  postcss.config.js

npm install
npm run dev

The preview runs React from a CDN and compiles JSX in the browser, which is
fine for previewing but awkward to keep working on. The export lifts the
component out, adds the imports the CDN build made unnecessary, and moves the
render call into main.jsx.

This was checked by generating a project and building it - npm install and
vite build both succeed, Tailwind compiles and React bundles.

Every other stack gets the split introduced in 0.1.8: separate
index.html, styles.css and script.js with a package.json. Anything that
doesn't look like a React page falls back to that too.

name: shot2code v0.1.8
body_html:
Adds a project-folder export and fixes Open in CodePen.

Install

Existing installs update themselves. For a fresh install:

File Use
shot2code-0.1.8-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.8-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

If the installer seems to do nothing: right-click the .exe ->
Properties -> tick Unblock -> Apply.

New: download as a project folder

The download button now offers two options:

  • Single HTML file - one self-contained page plus its images, as before
  • Project folder - index.html, styles.css and script.js as separate
    files, with a package.json and README so it runs with npm run dev

CDN tags stay in the HTML, and inline <script type="module"> blocks are left
where they are, because moving them would break module loading for the Preact
and Material stacks.

Fixed

Open in CodePen was broken three ways:

  • It assumed every page used Tailwind and only knew about Ionic, so Bootstrap,
    Bulma, daisyUI, Alpine and htmx pens opened without their framework. The
    externals are now taken from what the page actually uses.
  • A stray space in the Tailwind URL produced a malformed list.
  • In the desktop app the pen opened empty. CodePen is opened by submitting
    a form, and handing that to the system browser dropped the submitted code.

The exported zip is also named shot2code-export.zip rather than carrying the
old project name.

name: shot2code v0.1.7
body_html:
Doubles the number of output stacks, and auto-update now works.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.7-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.7-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

If the installer seems to do nothing: Windows blocks downloaded files.
Right-click the .exe -> Properties -> tick Unblock -> Apply.

This is the last release you should need to install by hand. From here the
app checks for updates on launch, downloads in the background and offers to
restart.

New stacks

Six more output targets, bringing the total to twelve:

Stack Good for
Alpine.js + Tailwind Interactive pages without a framework
Preact + Tailwind React-style components, a fraction of the size
Tailwind + daisyUI Ready-made components on top of Tailwind
Bulma Clean CSS framework, no utility classes
Material 3 Google's Material Design components
htmx + Tailwind Hypermedia-driven interactions

Alongside the existing HTML+Tailwind, HTML+CSS, React, Vue, Bootstrap and Ionic.

Every stack has to run as a single self-contained HTML file, so each CDN was
checked before being offered. Svelte was considered and left out: its components
must be compiled, which cannot happen in the page.

Fixed

  • Auto-update could have installed a corrupt file. Tagging a release also
    triggered a CI build that republished it, which left the update manifest
    describing a binary that was no longer attached. Releases are now published
    from a single verified build, and CI only checks that the app still packages.

Getting started

Run gh auth login (or copilot) once, then pick your models in Settings.

name: shot2code v0.1.6
body_html:
Video and screen recordings now work through GitHub Copilot - no Gemini key required.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.6-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.6-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

If the installer seems to do nothing: Windows blocks downloaded files.
Right-click the .exe -> Properties -> tick Unblock -> Apply.

New: video via Copilot

Previously a screen recording required a Gemini API key. Now, if you have
Copilot models selected in Settings, recordings work on your Copilot
subscription instead.

How it works. Copilot offers Gemini models, but its SDK cannot accept video
directly - a video attachment reaches the model as nothing at all. shot2code
therefore samples the recording into frames and sends them as an ordered
sequence of images, which the model reads correctly.

Which is used:

  • Gemini key present - still the default for video. Gemini reads video
    natively at a real frame rate and understands motion in more detail.
  • Copilot models selected, no Gemini key - Copilot is used.

Worth knowing: frame sampling is coarser than native video. For screen
recordings of a UI it works well, since what matters is the states the
interface passes through. For anything motion-heavy, Gemini remains better.

While generating from a recording, the agent's own screenshot-preview step is
skipped, because Copilot limits how many images one request may contain.

Getting started

Run gh auth login (or copilot) once, then pick your models in Settings.

name: shot2code v0.1.5
body_html:
Fixes the blank Settings page. If you are on v0.1.4 or earlier, please upgrade.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.5-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.5-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

If the installer seems to do nothing: Windows blocks downloaded files.
Right-click the .exe -> Properties -> tick Unblock -> Apply, or
use More info -> Run anyway on the SmartScreen prompt.

Fixed

  • Settings opened to a blank window, and Copilot models were never listed.
    Saved settings replaced the app's defaults wholesale, so a settings file
    written before the model list existed left that field missing, and reading it
    threw while drawing the page. React then tore down the whole screen, which
    also made the logo and preview controls appear dead. Stored settings are now
    merged over the defaults, so older saved state keeps working and adding a
    setting can no longer break an existing install.

  • A crash used to leave a completely blank window with nothing to go on.
    There is now an error screen with Reload and Reset settings and reload.

New: pick models anywhere

Copilot model selection was only in Settings. It is now also on the Upload,
URL and Text tabs, and in the modification toolbar next to the
design-system picker, so you can switch models while iterating.

It lists the models your Copilot plan actually offers and hides any that cannot
read images. "Auto" means shot2code chooses.

Screen recording intentionally has no model picker: video generation requires a
Gemini key.

Getting started

No API key needed with a GitHub Copilot subscription - run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks it up.

name: shot2code v0.1.4
body_html:
Adds screen recording, auto-update groundwork, and a full documentation refresh.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.4-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.4-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

Windows will warn you. These builds are not code-signed. Click
More info -> Run anyway, or right-click the file -> Properties ->
tick Unblock -> Apply. If the installer appears to do nothing, that
block is usually why.

Fixed

  • "Could not start screen recording". Screen capture is rejected in the
    desktop shell unless the app answers the request for a display source. It now
    does, preferring the Windows picker so you choose what to share. Verified
    end to end.

New

  • Auto-update. The app checks for updates on launch, downloads in the
    background and offers to restart.

    Heads-up: this cannot work while the repository is private, because release
    downloads need an authorization token that a shipped app cannot hold safely.
    It fails quietly and never blocks startup. Making the repository public would
    switch it on.

Documentation

Everything was rewritten to describe what shot2code actually is now - a Windows
desktop app - rather than the run-from-source project it started as. README,
Troubleshooting and Testing are current, and the last references to the
upstream project's owner, private SaaS repo and hosted service are gone.

Getting started

No API key needed with a GitHub Copilot subscription - run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks it up. Pick your models in Settings.

name: shot2code v0.1.3
body_html:
Fixes several issues that only showed up in the packaged desktop app, and adds a GitHub Copilot model picker.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.3-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.3-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

SmartScreen: not code-signed, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC". Click More info then Run anyway.

New: choose your Copilot models

shot2code now asks your Copilot plan which models it offers and lists them in
Settings. Tick the ones you want and each generation produces one variant per
selected model; leave them all unchecked to keep the automatic behaviour.
Models that cannot read images are hidden, since screenshot-to-code needs
image input. The built-in list grew from 12 to 24 models across Claude, GPT,
Gemini, Grok and MAI.

Fixed

  • Broken image icon in the sidebar. The logo used an absolute path, which
    points at the drive root when the UI is loaded from disk.
  • Window title said "Screenshot to Code".
  • Preview "open in new tab" did nothing. The preview opens a blob: URL,
    which was being handed to the OS browser that cannot open that scheme. Real
    external links still open in your browser.
  • Popped-out previews had broken relative URLs, caused by a base tag built
    from an origin that is null when running from disk.
  • Settings said API keys were "stored in your browser" - they are stored on
    this device.

Getting started

No API key needed with a GitHub Copilot subscription - run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks it up.

name: shot2code v0.1.2
body_html:
Fixes the blank window. v0.1.0 and v0.1.1 launched to an empty app - please upgrade.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.2-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.2-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

SmartScreen: not code-signed, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC".
Click More info then Run anyway.

Fixed

  • Blank window on launch. The desktop build loads the UI from disk over
    file://, where the path is the file's location (/C:/.../index.html)
    rather than /. The router matched no route, so nothing rendered even
    though the backend was running normally. The app now uses hash routing when
    loaded from disk.
  • A blank window produced no diagnostic. Renderer load failures, crashes and
    console errors are now written to the log file.

Earlier fixes, also included

  • Backend no longer exits when the bundled Chromium is missing or unreadable.
  • Splash screen during the ~60s cold start instead of no feedback.

Getting started

No API key needed with a GitHub Copilot subscription - run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks it up. Copilot models appear in the
picker prefixed with Copilot:. Otherwise add an OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini
key in Settings.

name: shot2code v0.1.1
body_html:
Fixes a defect in v0.1.0 and makes startup visible. Please upgrade from v0.1.0.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.1-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer
shot2code-0.1.1-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe

SmartScreen: these builds are not code-signed, so Windows shows
"Windows protected your PC". Click More info then Run anyway.

Fixed

  • Backend could die on startup. If the bundled Chromium was missing or
    unreadable (antivirus quarantine, incomplete extraction), the backend exited
    instead of disabling the screenshot-preview tool. The error handler itself
    crashed while logging, because the message contained non-ASCII characters
    that could not be encoded to the console codepage. v0.1.0 shipped a backend
    built before this fix. Verified: with Chromium absent, the backend now starts
    and reports screenshot_preview: false.
  • App looked hung for ~70 seconds on launch. A cold start boots Python and
    probes Chromium and Copilot before the window appeared. A splash screen now
    shows immediately.
  • Startup health check hammered the backend, because it polled an endpoint
    that blocks while spawning the Copilot CLI. Added a dedicated lightweight
    health endpoint.

Getting started

No API key needed with a GitHub Copilot subscription - run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks it up. Copilot models appear in the
picker prefixed with Copilot:. Otherwise add an OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini
key in Settings.

name: shot2code v0.1.0
body_html:
First release of shot2code - convert screenshots, mockups and recordings into clean code using AI.

Install

File Use
shot2code-0.1.0-x64.exe Recommended. Windows installer (choose install location, creates shortcuts)
shot2code-0.1.0-x64.zip Portable - unzip and run shot2code.exe, no install

Everything runs on your machine. Screenshots and API keys never leave it.

SmartScreen warning: these builds are not code-signed yet, so Windows will show
"Windows protected your PC". Click More info then Run anyway.

Getting started

No API key needed if you have a GitHub Copilot subscription - just run gh auth login
(or copilot) once and shot2code picks up that sign-in automatically. Copilot models
appear in the picker prefixed with Copilot:.

Otherwise add an OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key in Settings.

What's included

  • GitHub Copilot as a model provider (Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok through one sign-in)
  • OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini providers via your own API keys
  • Bundled Chromium so the agent can screenshot and visually check its own output
  • Stacks: HTML+Tailwind, HTML+CSS, React, Vue, Bootstrap, Ionic

Notes

  • Windows x64 only for now.
  • First launch takes a few seconds while the backend starts.

name: shot2code v0.3.1
body_html:
shot2code v0.3.1

Local-first Windows desktop app that turns screenshots, recordings, descriptions, and imported projects into editable web code using GitHub Copilot and other providers.

Highlights

  • Persistent local SQLite history, retry ancestry, and chat context.
  • Multi-file editor, nested project tree, safe sandboxed preview, and complete project export.
  • Folder/ZIP/source import and explicit multi-screenshot modes.
  • Twelve verified output stacks with stack-aware CodePen and Vite exports.
  • Redesigned responsive workspace with collapsible Chat/file panels and safe source formatting.
  • Corrected updater lifecycle that stops the frozen backend before one silent installer runs.

Source and full release notes: https://github.com/ArasaniRohithReddy/shot2code/releases/tag/v0.3.1

Downloads

  • shot2code-0.3.1-x64.exe — recommended per-user installer with automatic updates.
  • shot2code-0.3.1-x64.msi — per-machine managed deployment.
  • shot2code-0.3.1-x64.zip — portable build.
  • SHA256SUMS.txt — checksum verification.

The Windows binaries are currently unsigned and may trigger SmartScreen.
